requirements.source: S0 adversarial review F8; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (market windows are promises in real time); ADR-0002 decision 2; commits dfc0a13 (ran the catch-up market at 1x, wrong) and f999618 (its revert); code-architecture-game-2 m3; ADR-0016 decision 3
requirements.description: The offline catch-up keeps the saved market speed (marketTimeScale is not forced to 1x during the grace), so a bid made while the player was away keeps most of its window, which is set in real time at the saved speed (at least BID_MIN_OPEN_HOURS, about 3 real minutes), once play resumes at that speed. Catch-up time uses up part of the window: a bid the least patient buyer makes early in the 12-game-hour catch-up has about 2.5 real minutes left at 3x and about 3 at 10x, which the owner accepted as it is (ADR-0016 decision 3).
acceptance: marketTimeScale returns the saved speed while offlineGrace is set

For games saved at 3x and 10x, after six real hours away (a 12-game-hour catch-up), every bid created during the catch-up and still open on return has at least the minimum the code guarantees left at the saved speed: about 2.5 real minutes at 3x and about 3 at 10x (worst cases about 148 s and 176 s: a 0.1-patience buyer's bid made at the start of the catch-up; ADR-0016 decision 3), and the check sees real buyer activity
requirements.note: code-architecture-game-2 m3: tests/sim/fix-econ-offline-market-speed.test.ts asserts at least 171 real seconds (180 × 0.95) at both speeds, more than the code guarantees at 3x (about 148 s); it passes on its seeds 11-15, and the review found seed 116 failing it. ADR-0016 decision 3 allows aligning that 3x check with the documented minimum as a reviewed test change (it must assert what the code guarantees, never less); until then the test is stricter than A2.

requirements.source: design §10.3 (when it runs, daily change, weekly scrape, determinism), §21 Phase 3 Done when (automation tests; water, staff, determinism and step-invariance tests stay green); master §9 S3-A (deterministic daily water changes; weekly glass cleaning; offline/catch-up correctness); umbrella AUTO-001
requirements.description: runWaterChanger, called right after runAutofeeder in stepTankWaterImpl for a device that is on and not failed, finds each crossing of the tank's lights-on hour (tank.lighting?.onHour ?? 8) inside [ctx.hour, ctx.hour + dt), changes setting ?? 0.1 of the water with matched temperature when at least 20 game hours have passed since water.lab.lastAutoChangeHour, scrapes the glass when at least 168 have passed since water.lab.lastAutoScrapeHour, uses no RNG, is step-size invariant and runs during offline catch-up.

equipmentSummary() fills waterChanger the way it fills autofeeder, and the sudden-change (shock) check still applies to device changes.

simulateOffline across a lights-on hour performs the change without the device failing during the offline grace (fix-water-grace-equipment stays green), and core-determinism and fix-core-step-invariance stay green.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D Tier 3 (feed production); ADR-0002 decision 4; umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: At least one deterministic, facility-scale feed-production chain suited to species needs (for example live-feed culture, prepared feed batches or hatch/culture cycles) with storage capacity, consumption rates and shortage behaviour, using resource names reconciled with the current inventory and food data.
acceptance: Before implementation, a reconnaissance note maps the chain's inputs and outputs to existing food ids and inventory fields, so no resource is invented where an existing one fits.
A culture or batch cycle turns tracked inputs into tracked feed on a game-time schedule, capped by storage capacity.
Autofeeders or keepers consume the produced feed at defined rates, and running out shows a shortage instead of silently skipping.
Copy, test ids and player-facing resource names come from the approved DESIGN-S3D.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D Tier 4 (breeding facility); ADR-0002 decision 4; umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: The breeding-facility tier is the S3-C production lines integrated into the facility layer: multiple lines, nursery/grow-out routing, trait-based sorting, quarantine scheduling, protected keepers, automatic listing and capacity-aware pausing, each reported to the operations control.
acceptance: Each Tier 4 item maps to a GREEN PROD requirement: multiple lines PROD-002, routing PROD-006, sorting PROD-013, quarantine PROD-007, keepers PROD-008 and PROD-011, listing PROD-012, pausing PROD-010.
Every line's status, per-line throughput and bottlenecks appear in the Tier 5 operations overview through the surfaces DESIGN-S3D approves.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D Tier 5 (operations control); ADR-0002 decision 4; umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: A facility automation overview shows the status of every automated subsystem, bottleneck and shortage reports, per-line throughput, scheduling, pause/resume, an emergency/manual override and weekly economics.
acceptance: The overview lists every automated subsystem (Autofeeders, Auto Water Changers, reserves, feed chains, production lines) with its current status.
Pause/resume and the emergency override stop the targeted subsystem from the next simulation step, and manual care actions stay available while it is stopped.
Weekly economics sum automation costs and revenue from tracked ledger entries and match the finance ledger for the same week.
Copy and test ids come from the approved DESIGN-S3D.

Scheduling (master §9 S3-D Tier 5), proposed until DESIGN-S3D is approved: every scheduled automation run happens at its scheduled game time at most once per crossing, live and in the offline catch-up (AUTO-018, AUTO-023), a schedule the player changes takes effect from the next simulation step, and the operations control shows each subsystem's schedule; DESIGN_INTAKE.md step 6 replaces this with the approved design's concrete criterion before AUTO-015 leaves BLOCKED (requirements-3 R3-m4).

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D automation simulation rules (deterministic; game time, not render frames; variable step sizes; bounded offline catch-up; testable as pure simulation logic); master §5; umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: Every automation subsystem (the S3-A devices, the S3-C production lines and the S3-D chains) is pure, deterministic simulation logic in src/sim, driven by game time rather than render frames or the wall clock, giving the same outcome for any partition of a game-time span into steps and running inside bounded offline catch-up wherever it would run live.
acceptance: A seeded property test splits the same game-time span into random step sizes and gets the same automation outcomes and stateHash for each subsystem.

No automation code under src/sim uses Math.random, Date.now, performance.now or requestAnimationFrame (core-determinism-guard passes with its allow-list unchanged), and any randomness comes from ctx.rng or a subsystem's own persisted stream.
simulateOffline over a span gives the same automation results as live stepping over the same span.
Automation unit tests import only from src/sim, src/data and src/types (no React or DOM).

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D automation simulation rules (consume real tracked resources; never create money, animals, feed or supplies from nothing; surface shortages instead of silently skipping forever); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: Automation only consumes and produces tracked resources, so money, animals, feed, salt and supplies change only through recorded consumption, production, purchases, sales, births and deaths, and no job is skipped silently for lack of a resource.
acceptance: Over a long seeded run with every automation enabled, the change in money equals the sum of ledger entries, and food, salt and supply stocks equal their recorded inflows minus outflows.
The creature count changes only through recorded births, deaths, purchases and sales.

Each skip path records the shortage and emits a throttled notice the way design §10.3's out-of-salt notice does; any further surfacing (Alerts drawer rows, dashboard indicators) is as the approved DESIGN-S3D specifies.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D automation simulation rules (idempotent across retries/load boundaries; persist last-run markers where required); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: Every scheduled automation action records a persisted last-run marker in the save (such as water.lab.lastAutoChangeHour), so re-running a step over a game-time window that already ran, after a retry, a repair or a load, does nothing more.
acceptance: Running the automation step for a window and then again for the same window leaves the state unchanged on the second run.
Every marker is an optional, lane-tagged save field that repairState validates when present.
A save without a marker (an older save) triggers at most one catch-up action per job, never a burst.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D automation simulation rules (respect tank capacity and compatibility; preserve protected/Prismatic animals); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: No automation moves an animal into a tank the player's own move action would refuse, and none sells, lists or moves out of protection a Prismatic animal or a protected keeper.
acceptance: A property test over all automation finds no automated move into a tank that fails the environment gate or the stocking limit; production lines move animals only into the tanks validated at setup (design §11.1), and any further compatibility cut-off for automated moves is as the approved DESIGN-S3D specifies.
The same test finds no automated listing, sale or move that takes a Prismatic animal or an animal in a keep tank out of protection.
requirements.note: Needs owner or reviewer confirmation: master §9 S3-D says "preserve protected/Prismatic animals" without defining "protected"; whether the existing creature.favorite flag counts is UNKNOWN and needs an owner decision in the S3 contract.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D anti-dupe invariants (one creature cannot occupy two automation stages at once); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: At every step each creature belongs to at most one automation stage across all production lines and automation jobs, so it can't be one line's parent and another line's juvenile, or be in quarantine and kept at once.
acceptance: A property test over seeded multi-line runs checks after every step that no creature id appears in two stages.
Starting a line whose pair would put a creature into a second stage (for example a parent already used by another line) is refused.
requirements.note: Needs owner or reviewer confirmation: the design gives no copy for refusing such a line; the wording comes from DESIGN-S3C-LINES or the S3 contract.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D anti-dupe invariants (one creature cannot be sold/listed twice); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: A creature is in at most one active listing at a time and is sold at most once, whether the player or automation listed it.
acceptance: A property test finds, after every step, no creature id in two active listings and no sold creature in a later listing.
A line never lists a creature the player has already listed.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D anti-dupe invariants (one resource unit cannot be consumed twice); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: Each unit of food, salt, prepared water or other supply is consumed by at most one action, so two jobs due in the same step can't both spend the same stock.
acceptance: With stock for exactly one job and two jobs due in the same step, exactly one runs and the other reports a shortage.
No stock goes negative in any seeded run.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D anti-dupe invariants (one scheduled maintenance crossing cannot execute twice); design §10.3 (the 20 h and 168 h guards); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: Each scheduled maintenance crossing, such as a lights-on water change or a weekly scrape, executes at most once, even when a step boundary falls exactly on the crossing hour or the same window is stepped again.
acceptance: A step ending exactly at the lights-on hour followed by a step starting there performs one change, not two.
Re-stepping the same window after the change ran performs no second change (the 20 h and 168 h guards hold).

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D anti-dupe invariants (one clutch cannot be routed twice); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: Each clutch is moved to a raise tank at most once, by at most one line.
acceptance: A property test finds no clutch id that is the subject of two Move to nursery actions.
Two lines that share a tank never both route the same clutch.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D anti-dupe invariants (one listing cannot be generated twice from the same automation event); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: Each automation event that creates a listing, such as a juvenile finishing quarantine, creates exactly one listing even if the step is retried or the event is seen again.
acceptance: Re-running the step that ended a quarantine creates no second listing for the same juvenile.
In seeded runs, the number of automation listings equals the number of distinct quarantine completions with autoList on (Prismatic and kept animals excluded).

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D anti-dupe invariants (save/load does not repeat a completed job); master §9 S3-D automation simulation rules (never double-run an action after save/load); master §9 S3-C (restart-safe pipeline); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: Saving and loading at any point (mid-pipeline, just after a water change, just after a listing) never repeats a completed automation job or skips a due one.
acceptance: For each job type, a run that saves and loads right after the job completes ends with the same stateHash as an uninterrupted run.
A production line saved mid-quarantine resumes after loading with the same time left.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D anti-dupe invariants (repair/recovery cannot duplicate a line's output); design §15 (repairState for production); umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: Running repairState or recovering from a backup save never duplicates a line's output: no juvenile, nursery move, listing or statistic is created or counted twice.
acceptance: repairState applied to a save with a broken line creates no creature or listing and no stats increment.
Recovering from the backup slot and continuing gives the same line outputs as continuing from the main save, with no duplicate creature, listing or stat count.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-D (extended automation scope control); master §45; ADR-0001 (option C); ADR-0002 decision 4; umbrella AUTO-002
requirements.description: S3 may simplify an individual proposed machine but may not reduce extended automation to Auto-feed and Auto-clean, and any substantial reduction of S3-D is recorded in an ADR with the architectural blocker, independent reviewer agreement and, when the owner-visible experience changes, owner approval.
acceptance: requirements-audit.mjs refuses S3 acceptance while any of AUTO-012 to AUTO-015 is open, unless an owner-approved ADR closes it (SUPERSEDED with that decision).

Every simplification of a Tier 2-5 item has an ADR that names the blocker and records the reviewer's agreement, and an owner-visible reduction stops at OWNER_GATE with reason SCOPE_REDUCTION:<requirement id>.

requirements.source: master §9 S4 (whole-stack hardening: automation invariants); master §10 (automation invariants green)
requirements.description: On the final S4 tree every automation invariant (AUTO-016 to AUTO-027 and the PROD determinism and tolerance requirements) is re-run and GREEN.
acceptance: automation-invariants, automation-water-changer and production-line tests pass on the S4 tree.
The S4 report lists each invariant with its test and result.

requirements.source: design §12; master §9 S3-B; master §44
requirements.description: Implement truthful web notifications and approved quiet-hours/category behavior.
acceptance: Every requirement whose source names "umbrella NOTIFY-001" is closed: GREEN, DEFERRED or SUPERSEDED (requirements-audit.mjs refuses NOTIFY-001 GREEN while one is still open)
No copy promises alerts while the game is closed

requirements.source: design §12.2 (preferences; quiet hours), §12.3 item 3; master §3.10; ADR-0001; master §9 S3-B (device-local notification preferences; fixed 10 PM–8 AM quiet hours); umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: Notification preferences live only on the device, in localStorage 'aquarium-go.notify.v1' as {categories: Record<Category, boolean>, quiet: {on, start: 22, end: 8}} with Rare stock, Animal care, Market and Breeding on and Shows off by default, and quiet hours are fixed at 10:00 PM – 8:00 AM on the device clock with only an on/off switch (notify-quiet, on by default) and hold every notification except danger-level Animal care.
acceptance: Toggling a category or quiet hours writes the key and survives a reload, a missing or malformed value falls back to the defaults, and nothing about notifications enters the save or its stateHash.
notify-rules.test.ts: with quiet hours on, a Market event at 22:00 and at 07:59 is not shown, one at 08:00 is (proposed boundaries, see note), and a danger-level Animal care event at 23:00 is shown.
With quiet hours off, the same 23:00 Market event is shown.
The Quiet hours row reads '10:00 PM – 8:00 AM' / 'Urgent animal care still comes through' and offers no control to edit the hours.
requirements.note: Needs owner or reviewer confirmation: treating 22:00 as inside and 08:00 as outside quiet hours is a proposal (the design gives start 22 and end 8 only), and the design does not say whether held notifications are dropped or delivered when quiet hours end.

requirements.source: design §12.2 (categories table; rules), §21 Phase 3 Done when (notify-rules, notify-offer-events, notifications.spec); master §9 S3-B (categories); umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: Pure rules in src/ui/notify/rules.ts map GameEvents to {category, title, body, route, priority} per the design §12.2 table (Rare stock, Animal care, Market, Breeding and Shows results) with its exact title and body templates and routes, unmapped events never notify, and a switched-off category suppresses its events.
acceptance: notify-rules.test.ts asserts title, body and route per category, for example 'Prismatic {species} in the shop' to #/shop/fish/{offerId}, Auto-feed paused to #/tanks/{id}/equipment, illness to #/livestock/animal/{id}, a bid to #/market/listings/{id}, a hatch to #/livestock/eggs and a show result to #/shows/results.
An unmapped event returns no notification, and a category set to off produces none.
Danger-level Animal care events carry the priority that quiet hours let through.
requirements.note: Club-show reminders need the Social stub's clubs (S4); their route and dev-mode gating are tested with SOC-011 A5 in S4, not here (requirements-2 m8).

requirements.source: design §12.2 (event links need an offer id), §7.7, §15; umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: GameEvent gains an optional offerId (// lane:notify) that announcePrismatic, stockNewUnlocks and maybeSpecial set, so the rule routes those events to #/shop/fish/{offerId} (rare-stock events without one go to #/shop), and the Alerts drawer's link for a Prismatic stocking reads 'Open the shop'.
acceptance: notify-offer-events.test.ts: announcePrismatic and the special and new-unlock stock events set offerId, and the rule maps it to #/shop/fish/{offerId}, or to #/shop when absent.
The Alerts drawer entry for a Prismatic stocking links 'Open the shop' to #/shop/fish/<offerId>.

requirements.source: design §12.2 (rate limits; tag); master §9 S3-B (rate limiting); umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: System notifications are limited to one per category per 30 real minutes, with later ones folded into '… and {n} more' on the next one, and to six per real hour overall, and every notification of a category carries the same tag so the OS replaces rather than stacks them.
acceptance: notify-rules.test.ts with a fake clock: a second same-category event within 30 minutes is not shown, and the next one shown ends with 'and {n} more' counting the folded events.
The seventh notification within one real hour is not shown.
Every shown notification has tag equal to its category, and the limits run on real time, not game time.

requirements.source: design §12.1 (web vs app copy), §12.3, §12.5, §20.3 (tests that count Settings tabs); ADR-0003 (supersession register: the §12.3 iOS copy is an open owner question; native parts deferred); master §44; master §9 S3-B; umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: Settings gains the Notifications tab (General · Play & access · Saves · Notifications · About; #/settings/notifications; settings-tab-notifications) with the notify-status callout in web wording (the Unsupported state's copy as the owner decides), the 'This browser' row whose notify-test sends the §12.5 test notification, the five notify-cat-<id> category rows with their exact subtitles, disabled unless permission is granted, and the Quiet hours row.
acceptance: notifications.spec: with notifications granted and window.Notification stubbed, notify-turn-on leads to the granted callout, and notify-test records exactly one notification titled 'Test notification' after about 1.5 s, even with the page focused; when not granted, notify-test shows the toast 'Turn notifications on first'.

notify-status shows the §12.3 web callout for default, granted and denied, and for unsupported the copy the owner decides (recorded in an ADR); no 'app' variant ships, so no callout promises alerts while the game is closed (native wrapping is deferred, NOTIFY-011).
The notify-cat-<rare|care|market|breeding|shows> switches are aria-disabled, focusable and explained until permission is granted, and their subtitles match §12.2.
#/settings/notifications opens the tab (scrolled into view on phones), tests that count Settings tabs expect five, and save.spec stays green.
requirements.note: Needs owner or reviewer confirmation: the Unsupported callout copy (design §12.3's iOS 'add Aquarium Go to your Home Screen' sentence; §22 risk 5) is an open owner question (ADR-0003, master §44); the app has no manifest today.

requirements.source: design §12.4; master §9 S3-B (permission flow); umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: The game never asks for notification permission on launch: 'Turn on' in Settings › Notifications and in the Alerts drawer footer (alerts-notify-cta, shown only while permission is 'default') calls platform().notifications.request() from the click handler, a grant shows the info toast 'Notifications on' and applies the category defaults, a denial shows the Denied callout, and a dismissed prompt leaves 'Not asked'.
acceptance: No permission request happens during boot or play until a Turn on click (a spy on Notification.requestPermission stays at zero calls).
alerts-notify-cta shows only for permission default and opens #/settings/notifications.
A grant shows the 'Notifications on' info toast (copy exactly as design §16 specifies) and the granted callout; a denial shows 'Blocked in your browser'; a dismissal leaves 'Notifications are off'.

requirements.source: design §12.1, §12.6 (event source, when to show, content), §2 D13; master §44; master §9 S3-B (web notification delivery); umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: The notify module subscribes to new state.log entries (the stream Toasts uses), runs the rules, and shows a system notification only when permission is granted, the category is on, quiet hours don't hold it and document.visibilityState === 'visible' && !document.hasFocus(), each carrying the title, body, a 192px PNG app icon rendered from public/favicon.svg, tag = category and data.route, while toasts, emitEvent and the Alerts drawer stay the primary channel.
acceptance: With the page focused, an eligible event shows the in-game toast and no system notification.
Visible but unfocused, with permission granted and the category on, exactly one notification is shown with icon, tag and data.route set.
With the tab hidden nothing is shown, and no push subscription or push server is used anywhere.
A 192px PNG app icon exists under public/ and is the notification icon.

requirements.source: design §12.6 (service worker; on click), §15 (public/sw.js), §22 risk 3, §6.4; master §9 S3-B (service worker click routing; deep-link return); master §24; umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: A minimal hand-written public/sw.js (no build plugin, no dependency), registered at import.meta.env.BASE_URL + 'sw.js' with scope BASE_URL, handles only notificationclick by focusing an existing game window and posting {route} or opening BASE_URL + '#' + route, after which the game calls go(route, {fromNotification: true}), and a newly opened window goes through the §6.4 link boot before the route.
acceptance: sw.js registers only a notificationclick listener (no fetch, cache or push handlers), and its registration scope equals BASE_URL (/aquarium-go/ in the GitHub Pages build).
A unit test of sw.js with a fake clients API focuses and messages an open window, and opens BASE_URL#route when no window exists.
notifications.spec: opening a notification for an offer shows the offer with offer-from-notification visible, and a fresh window shows boot-deeplink before the offer.
The security/data review of the service-worker change is GREEN.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-B (notification evidence/testing); master §28; design §12.8; umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: S3 records objective notification evidence: the notify unit tests and notifications.spec with command, exit code and counts, plus browser screenshots of the Settings › Notifications tab in its default, granted, denied and unsupported states, the Alerts drawer footer, a system notification while unfocused, and an offer opened from a notification.
acceptance: evidence/S3/manifest.json lists notify-rules, notify-offer-events and notifications.spec runs with exit code 0 and pass counts.
Screenshots of each listed state at 1440×900 and 390×844 are recorded with path and SHA-256.
The browser/QA reviewer's verdict on these states is recorded in evidence/S3/reviews/.

requirements.source: design §12.7, §21 Phase 6, §20.1 (notify-forecast.test.ts), §2 D13, §12.3 ('app' variants); ADR-0001 (native wrapping deferred); ADR-0003 (supersession register: D13 native part, §12.7, Phase 6 and notify-forecast.test.ts DEFERRED); master §3.10; master §9 S3-B (closed/native notifications deferred); umbrella NOTIFY-001
requirements.description: Predicted notifications while the game is closed (forecasting the catch-up on a structuredClone of the game at app pause, scheduling at most 3 local notifications at +15 min and a +2 h digest shifted out of quiet hours, cancelling them on resume), and the §12.3 'app' copy variants that promise them, need the native wrapper and are deferred.
acceptance: No forecast or scheduling code, and no 'app' copy variant, ships in this program.

When un-deferred: notify-forecast.test.ts shows the forecast on a cloned state produces the same events as simulateOffline from the same state and leaves the original untouched, and a device test shows scheduled alerts that match the catch-up.

requirements.source: design §11; master §9 S3-C; master §3.10
requirements.description: Implement multiple deterministic production lines per species.
acceptance: Every requirement whose source names "umbrella PROD-001" is closed: GREEN, DEFERRED or SUPERSEDED (requirements-audit.mjs refuses PROD-001 GREEN while one is still open)
Two lines for the same species run side by side without sharing a creature, clutch or listing

requirements.source: design §11.2, §15, §21 Phase 5 Done when (production-line.test.ts and persistence-05 pass); master §3.10; ADR-0001; master §9 S3-C (multiple production lines per species); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: GameState gains the optional production?: ProductionState {lines: ProductionLine[]} (// lane:production; absent means no lines) with the design §11.2 ProductionLine shape (id, speciesId, pair, tanks {breed, raise, quarantine, keep}, running, rules {pauseWhenFull, keepPrismatic, autoList, keep[]}, stats?), and several lines may share a speciesId while staying independent.
acceptance: production-line.test.ts: two betta lines with different pairs and tanks progress independently over the same game days.
A fresh game has no production field and the same stateHash as before the change, and SCHEMA_VERSION is unchanged.
The new types are optional additions in src/types/game.ts tagged // lane:production.

requirements.source: design §11.1, §6.2 (#/livestock/production), §19 (Production); ADR-0003 (supersession register: several lines per species, the UI needs a design ADR before S3-C UI work); master §3.10; master §9 S3-C; umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: Livestock gains a fourth tab, 'Production', after Past residents (livestock-tab-production, #/livestock/production, target tab:production) that shows every line, its stages, tiles, status and rules, the empty state and the set-up flow as the approved DESIGN-S3C-LINES specifies, starting from design §11.1 for a single line.
acceptance: #/livestock/production opens the tab on desktop and phone, and the route round-trips.

Each line, including two or more lines of one species, renders with the header, tiles, stage cards, status badge and rule switches in the layout and copy DESIGN-S3C-LINES approves, with the stage and tile values (Quarantine count and days left, the Sort keep-rule chips, the Sell reserve line, Running or Paused shown with an icon and a word, the This week figure) taken from the line's live state.

The set-up flow offers only compatible adult pairs, validates tanks with the existing compatibility and stocking checks, collects the keep tank where DESIGN-S3C-LINES places that step, and Start line creates a running line.
The empty state and its Set up a line action, and how further lines are added once some exist, follow DESIGN-S3C-LINES.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-C (breeding pair); design §11.2 (pair), §11.3 (Breed); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: Each line names one breeding pair (pair.motherId, pair.fatherId), a compatible adult female and male of the line's species when the line starts, and processes only the clutches that pair lays.
acceptance: Starting a line with a non-adult, a same-sex pair or a pair of another species is refused.
A clutch laid by another pair in the same tank is never moved, sorted or listed by the line.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-C (breed tank); design §11.2 (tanks.breed), §11.3 (Breed); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: tanks.breed is the tank where the pair lives and spawns through the existing breeding simulation, and the line adds no new biology and never creates eggs itself.
acceptance: With the pair in the breed tank and breeding conditions met, clutches come only from the existing breeding simulation (no production code path creates a clutch).
Breeding of a pair that belongs to no line is unchanged, and lifecycle-genetics stays green.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-C (raise/grow-out tank); design §11.3 (Raise); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: When a clutch from the pair reaches 'Free-swimming fry', the line runs the existing 'Move to nursery' action into tanks.raise, exactly once per clutch.
acceptance: production-line.test.ts: fry move to the raise tank at the free-swimming stage and not before.
The move goes through the same code path and validation as the player's Move to nursery action.
If the move is refused (for example the raise tank is full), the fry stay where they are and the line records a notice naming the blocked stage.
requirements.note: Needs owner or reviewer confirmation: design §11.3 does not say what happens when the raise tank is full and pauseWhenFull is off, and gives no copy for the notice; keeping the fry in place with a notice is a proposal for the S3 contract or DESIGN-S3C-LINES.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-C (quarantine tank); design §11.3 (Quarantine), §11.1 (stage 4); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: Juveniles not kept at the Sort stage move to tanks.quarantine and are held there for 7 game days before the Sell stage.
acceptance: A juvenile entering quarantine becomes eligible for the Sell stage after exactly 168 game hours, whatever the step size.
Before its hold ends a quarantined juvenile is never listed or moved by the line, even with autoList on.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-C (safe/keeper tank); design §11.2 (tanks.keep), §11.3 (Sort), §11.1 (rule subline); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: tanks.keep is the line's safe tank: with keepPrismatic on, every Prismatic youngster moves there instead of to quarantine, and the line never moves an animal out of it to quarantine or a listing.
acceptance: With keepPrismatic on, a Prismatic juvenile moves to the keep tank at the Sort stage.
No animal in the keep tank is ever moved to quarantine or listed by the line.
requirements.note: Needs owner or reviewer confirmation: design §11.3 says the Sort stage "keeps" juveniles matching the trait rules without saying where they go (only Prismatic ones are sent to the keep tank); the destination needs an owner decision in the S3 contract.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-C (running/paused state); design §11.1 (header switch and status badge); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: line.running is set by the production-toggle switch ('{Species} line running'); a paused line moves, sorts and lists nothing, and resuming continues the pipeline from where it stopped.
acceptance: Over several game days a paused line performs no move, sort or listing.
Resuming continues the pipeline without repeating or skipping a stage.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-C (pause-when-full rule); design §11.3 (Breed), §11.1 (rule row); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: With pauseWhenFull on, while the raise tank is at its stocking limit the line stops the pair from spawning, through the tank's breedingEnv conditions or by parking one parent in tanks.keep (chosen after reading the breeding module), until there is room again.
acceptance: production-line.test.ts 'pauses when full': no new clutch is laid while the raise tank is at its stocking limit.
Spawning resumes once the raise tank has room, and a parked parent (if that mechanism is chosen) returns to the breed tank.
The chosen mechanism is recorded in the S3 slice contract or an ADR.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-C (never-sell-Prismatic rule); design §11.3 (Sell), §11.1 (rule row); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: A production line never lists or sells a Prismatic animal, whatever its rule switches say, and the 'Never sell Prismatic animals' switch (keepPrismatic) also moves Prismatic youngsters to the keep tank.
acceptance: production-line.test.ts 'never lists Prismatic': across seeded runs with Prismatic juveniles, no listing references a Prismatic creature, with keepPrismatic on or off.
With keepPrismatic off, a Prismatic juvenile is still never listed.
requirements.note: Needs owner or reviewer confirmation: with keepPrismatic off the design gives a Prismatic juvenile no destination, so it would stay in quarantine indefinitely; the owner should decide where it goes.

requirements.source: master §9 S3-C (automatic listing rule); design §11.3 (Sell), §11.1 (rule row); umbrella PROD-001
requirements.description: With autoList on, the day quarantine ends each juvenile is listed through the existing listing code as kind 'Juveniles', and with autoList off the line creates no listing.

requirements.description: Forward safety: the save code this build ships never treats a save written by newer code (schemaVersion above its own SCHEMA_VERSION, 'too_new') as damaged, never falls back past it to an older backup or another backend's copy, never rotates it away and never overwrites it, so a later format change can't destroy progress; the new data shapes this build adds are validated on load; well-formed records a newer build added under the same schema are kept (PERSIST-011); and a newer build that adds a species or a tank size raises SCHEMA_VERSION, so older builds treat its saves as too_new (ADR-0016 decision 2). A schema change is allowed when a feature needs it, documented and tested (master §3.5).
acceptance: A slot whose primary record is too_new loads as too_new, not as damaged: the game restores neither the slot's .backup nor another backend's copy, and doesn't tell the player the save is damaged
saveGame, the synchronous pagehide/hidden write and the backup rotation never rotate out or overwrite a record whose header or body schemaVersion is above SCHEMA_VERSION
Every data shape this build adds to the save is validated on load by repairState: a malformed value is repaired with a note, never trusted (PERSIST-006, PERSIST-007, PERSIST-011)
Any SCHEMA_VERSION change ships with its migration, a test that loads the previous version, and a docs entry (master §3.5)

A save written by a newer build under the same SCHEMA_VERSION, carrying equipment, decor, stored and listed frag, research and starter ids this build doesn't know, loads with repairs: [] and every such record exactly as saved, round-trips save → load → save with an equal stateHash and nothing to repair, needs no second repair, and the world steps 24 game hours around it keeping the equipment, decor, frags and starter (core-forward-compat.test.ts: "PERSIST-003 / PERSIST-011: a newer save keeps the catalog ids this build does not know"); the research step still closes an active project this build doesn't know (see the note)

A change that adds a species to the species registry (ALL_SPECIES, src/data/species) or a tank size to the tank catalog (TANK_TIERS, src/data/catalog/tanks.ts) also raises SCHEMA_VERSION (src/persistence/schema.ts), with A4's migration, test and docs entry, so an older build treats a save holding the new content as too_new (A1-A2) instead of loading it; older builds don't keep unknown species or tank sizes inert (ADR-0016 decision 2). From S1, core-save-forward-safety.test.ts fails when one is added without the bump (PERSIST-014 A5); until then each slice's reviewers check git diff <last checkpoint, or the baseline>..<candidate> -- src/data/species src/data/catalog/tanks.ts src/persistence/schema.ts

requirements.description: mutateFast is atomic like useGame.mutate: when its recipe throws, nothing is published, so a world step that fails part-way never becomes the game state, is never built on by the next tick and is never autosaved; runTick keeps the failed tick's hours in its backlog instead of dropping them. When the publish itself throws (share() failing, or a store subscriber), the working copy is dropped too, so the next call starts from the store; and mutateFast is not re-entrant: a call from inside a running recipe is refused before it touches anything.
acceptance: A mutateFast recipe that throws leaves the store's game object, its version and every value unchanged, and the next call starts from the store, not from the abandoned working copy
runTick on a world step that throws changes nothing, counts one error in the loop stats and returns the tick's game hours as backlog

A publish that throws before the store update leaves the store's game object unchanged and nothing behind, so the next call starts from the store; a store subscriber that throws after the update leaves that update standing once, and the next call builds on it (core-fastmutate-atomic.test.ts: "a publish that throws before the store update leaves nothing behind: the next call starts from the store", "a store subscriber that throws after the update: the update stands once, and the next call builds on it")

A mutateFast call from inside a running recipe is refused ("not re-entrant") before it touches anything: an outer recipe that catches the refusal, or an inner failure, publishes only its own changes, and one that lets the refusal propagate publishes nothing, after which the next call works (core-fastmutate-atomic.test.ts: "a call from inside a running recipe is refused before it touches anything; the outer call stays atomic", "an outer recipe that lets the refusal propagate publishes nothing, and the next call works")
